title: Research audit: sharp fixed-a Gaussian envelope for balanced assembly (no new kappa)
head: de07c015b38e5b157016db636f210c4f7f537058
body:
PR294 proves a constructive sufficient region with effective bit parameter `a < 1/3`, while the existing domain audit identifies an independent Gaussian cap. This **research note / mathematical audit** gives the exact fixed-`a` arithmetic envelope for the same pinned historical balanced formula after omitting only `b_below_one_over32`:

- `M(a) = a/(1+a)` for `0 < a <= 1/3`;
- `M(a) = (1-2a)/(4a)` for `1/3 < a < 1/2`;
- no positive feasible target for `a >= 1/2` in this formula.

Every rational `0 < kappa < M(a)` has an explicit rational witness, assuming the stated leaf ordering and positive abstract bridge gaps. The proof uses `t=1-2h` and the identity `1/4-r = t[1-a(2+t)]/[4(1+at)]`. It extends PR294's scope; it does not identify an error in that proof. A stronger supplier can choose a smaller effective `a`, so the decreasing branch is not a supplier impossibility result.

**No new kappa or multiplication algorithm is claimed.** The production cap, selected #626/#543 certificate, `upstream/`, and all existing files remain unchanged. Actual bridge validity, supplier availability, and all compiler, hosting, recursion, precision, tape and analytic obligations remain outside this arithmetic result. This is not a formal proof of the multiplication theorem.

Four new files under `research/balanced-gaussian-envelope/` provide the proof, an exact standard-library verifier, a deterministic receipt, and source/provenance pins. The verifier executes the unchanged pinned assembly function with an explicitly assumed bridge and compares all 47 fractions against a separate factored calculation. It retains rejected cap rows and scalar precondition failures in the evidence.

Validation:

```sh
python3 -B research/balanced-gaussian-envelope/verify.py
# PASS_SCOPED_BALANCED_GAUSSIAN_ENVELOPE cases=7965 witnesses=288 controls=12
python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_assembly_domain.py -v
# 7 tests pass
make selected-record-check
# PASS; selected kappa remains 51110230636731/31250000000000000
```

The new receipt matches on Python 3.11, 3.14 and 3.15. A clean temporary copy with only the four added files and the one pinned assembly source also passes when launched outside the repository. Boundary cases approach the thresholds with 60-digit rational precision; controls cover Gaussian/target/leaf equality, bridge gaps, the production cap, scalar preconditions, Gaussian-row omission and source drift. The written argument supplies the universal result; finite replay is supporting evidence. `git diff --check` passes. Full `make verify` and the selected supplier cold replay were not run for this isolated research addition; remote CI is separate.

Base: `66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60`. Assignment seed **60**, adversarial mathematical audit. No pinned coordination issue existed, so the claim was recorded locally. A pre-submission refresh of 518 open PRs found no title-level overlap for this exact envelope; PR294 and PR657 remained at their recorded heads. PR657's broader pass/accounting ceiling is distinct and is not used as a theorem dependency.
